fields.meta_description: Build a tournament registration form that collects entry fees at sign-up and moves the next team to a waitlist once a division fills.
fields.h1: Build a Tournament Registration Form With Fees and Waitlists
fields.hero_description: Get a tournament registration form that takes entry fees at sign-up and saves every roster to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Sorts Out Before Play Starts
fields.features_subheading: Emailed sign-ups end up in a spreadsheet someone sorts by hand. Each part below does a piece of that sorting as a team registers.
fields.feature_1:
Rosters with a minimum and a maximum

Set how many players a team must list and how many it may carry, such as 7 and 12 for youth soccer. A roster outside those numbers stays unsent until the captain fixes it.
fields.feature_2:
Divisions with their own caps

Split the field by age group or skill level, and give each division a cap. Once a division fills, the form marks it full, and the next team to pick it joins a waitlist.
fields.feature_3:
Entry fees paid at sign-up

Connect Stripe, and the captain pays the team fee, or each player pays their own, as part of registering. Each team's row shows whether its fee is paid, and on what date.
fields.feature_4:
Parent approval for younger players

Ask for each player's birth date and a parent's email. When the birth date puts a player under 18, the app holds the spot and emails the parent a link to approve it.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts when a division fills

Once a division is full, the tournament director hears about it by email or in Slack. Captains who still owe a fee get an email reminder 7 days before registration closes.
fields.feature_6:
Every sign-up in a database you own

Each registration saves as a row in a database you own, and responses have no cap. Sort the rows by division to draw brackets and print the check-in list for the desk.

fields.usecase_heading: Golf, Soccer, Esports, and Chess Sign-Ups
fields.tab_content_1:
Each foursome pays $600 when it registers

Copper Basin Boosters charge $150 a golfer for their May 16 charity scramble. Captain Bronwyn Haverkamp enters her foursome with handicaps of 12, 18, 9, and 19, then pays $600 through Stripe. Tournament chair Lucian Brisbois gets an email with the paid foursome and its combined handicap of 58.
fields.tab_content_2:
Any U12 team after the 16th joins a waitlist

The Lanternfly Cup takes 16 teams in its U12 youth soccer division. Granite Falls FC registers as the 16th, and U12 shows as full on the form. Hollis Gap United registers next and lands on the waitlist. Tournament director Callista Ruelas gets a Slack direct message that U12 is full.
fields.tab_content_3:
One parent signs off on each player under 18

Ignacio Zubrin is 16 and signs up for the Glasswing Spring Cup, an online esports tournament, under the gamer tag VoltRiver. Because he is under 18, his spot waits. His mother, Lorena Zubrin, gets an email asking her to approve it, and the spot is confirmed once she does.
fields.tab_content_4:
Ratings sort each player into one of four sections

The Tern Harbor Chess Open splits its field into four sections: Under 1000, Under 1400, Under 1800, and Open. Soraya Ostrowski enters a rating of 1450, and the app places her in Under 1800. She gets an email with her section and the 9 a.m. start of round 1.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Tournament Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a tournament registration form that fills each division and collects every entry fee.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Set the divisions and their caps
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for what game day needs
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the entry fee and who pays it
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every division you will run, such as U10 and U12 or beginner and advanced, with a cap your fields and your schedule can carry. A division with no cap keeps taking teams after the bracket is drawn.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask only for what the event uses: jersey colors for soccer, handicaps for a golf scramble, ratings for chess, gamer tags for esports. Add a birth date whenever a division has an age limit.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide whether one fee covers the whole roster or every player owes a share. Connect Stripe so the fee is paid during registration instead of collected in cash at the check-in table.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the division, the first start time, and the check-in location in the confirmation email. Captains forward it to players who never saw the form. Keep it short.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the director an alert when a division fills, and send the treasurer a daily list of unpaid entries. Pick email or Slack for each alert, based on where that person already works.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit one team that fills a division, one with a player aged 16, and one that skips the fee. Check that each lands where it should before you share the link.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share the link and watch the counts
fields.howto_step_7_des: Post the link where your teams already look, such as last year's captains list or the league newsletter. Check the division counts each week and move a division's cap if the field allows it.

faq_plan.q: What is a tournament registration form?
faq_plan.a: A tournament registration form is the sign-up form a team or a player fills in to enter a tournament. It records who is playing and in which division, and it gives the organizer one list to draw the brackets from.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a tournament registration form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the tournament to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English, including the divisions with their caps and the entry fee. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, and you change any part by asking in the next prompt. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a golf tournament registration form ask each player?
faq_plan.a: A golf tournament registration form should ask each player for a name, a phone number, and a handicap, and ask the captain to list the foursome when teams register together. Add a shirt size if players get a shirt, and a meal choice if a dinner follows the round. If handicap is optional, ask for an average score instead, which still lets you balance the flights.

faq_plan.q: What should a youth tournament registration form ask parents?
faq_plan.a: Ask a parent or guardian for a name and a phone number, and ask for an emergency contact who will not be at the event. Add an optional field for allergies or medical notes the coach should see. A daycare registration form goes further, with pickup authorizations and daily schedules; a weekend tournament needs only what the staff would use on the day.

faq_plan.q: How do I cap each division on a tournament registration form?
faq_plan.a: Set a maximum for each division when you describe the form, such as 16 teams for U12. Pick a cap that fits your bracket: 8 or 16 teams fill a single-elimination bracket with no byes, while 12 teams leave 4 byes in round 1. If a team drops out, offer its spot to the first team on the waitlist. Emergent puts no response cap on the form, so the only limit is yours.

faq_plan.q: Can a tournament registration form charge an early-bird entry fee?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Set two prices and a cutoff date, such as $450 a team through March 1 and $525 after it, and the form charges whichever price applies on the day the team registers. Show both prices and the cutoff on the form, where captains can see what an early entry saves them.

faq_plan.q: When should a tournament registration form close?
faq_plan.a: Close it on the day you need the final count, then count back the time the brackets and the schedule take. If the schedule takes 3 days to build and teams should have it a week ahead, close registration 10 days before the first game. A conference registration form can stay open until the doors open: one more attendee changes nothing, while one more team changes the schedule.

faq_plan.q: Can players sign a waiver on a tournament registration form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add the waiver text as a step before payment, and have each player, or a parent for a player under 18, sign in a signature box. Emergent builds that step into the form, and the app saves each signature with its date on the player's row. Get the waiver's wording from your league or a lawyer: the form records the signature but does not decide what the waiver covers.

faq_plan.q: What does a gaming tournament registration form need?
faq_plan.a: A gaming tournament registration form needs each player's gamer tag and the platform they play on, plus an in-game rank if you seed players by skill. Ask for a time zone when players join online from different places. For team games, ask each team for a captain and one substitute, in case a player cannot make the start time.

faq_plan.q: Should a tournament registration form sign up a whole roster or each player?
faq_plan.a: Sign up a whole roster when a team plays as a unit, and have the captain list every player. Sign up each player when results are individual, as in a chess open, or when you pair single golfers into foursomes yourself. A summer camp registration form follows the per-person pattern. Either way, the app saves each entry to a database you own.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, Fluent Forms, Typeform, formNX, pdfFiller), a printable PDF and a help article for one tournament app. Each template stops at a team name, a roster and a contact. This page shows what an organizer needs once sign-ups start: a golf foursome that pays its entry fee at registration, a youth soccer division that closes at its cap and keeps a waitlist, an esports player under 18 who waits for a parent's approval, and a chess open that places each player in a section by rating. The FAQ covers the definition, how to build one, golf and gaming versions, parent details, division caps, early-bird fees, when to close, waivers, and team versus individual sign-up.
